resources.string: Choose songs (several at once is fine)
No program is making sound in the volume mixer right now. Start the one you want, then press again.
Other devices play by themselves once they connect to this one
If another computer cannot connect to this one, type: %1$s
%1$s is on none of this computer\'s networks (this computer: %2$s). If it will not connect, check first that the two are on the same network.
This computer is No. %1$d on the host\'s list
The host set SoundMesh\'s volume here to %1$d%% (the computer\'s own volume is untouched).
The host arranges this drawing; here it can only be looked at. The one with the outer ring is this computer.
Not receiving audio; it may have dropped
Drag each icon to where that device really is. “You” is the listener, and up is the front.
Devices on the left play the left channel and those on the right the right, split by the layout above.
The source circles around you; better with three devices or more.
Drag the ringed dot in the room drawing above to move the source.
The source sits on the ring of devices; the room is as it was.
The source is inside the ring of devices: direction is %1$d%% weaker.

But Room reverb is at zero right now, so pulling the source back only makes it quieter. Loudness alone cannot say how far away something is — a whisper at your ear and a shout across the street can be equally loud. Turn up Room reverb under Fine tuning: the reverb does not recede with the source, so one drops and the other does not, and the ear reads that as distance.
How much each device keeps once the sound turns away.
Click an icon in the room drawing to change which half it plays (it is written under the icon).
The computer plays at the volume set here * its own volume. If it is not loud enough, turn up the computer\'s own volume
This computer is not on a local network, so no phone or computer can reach it. Join a WiFi network or plug in a cable first.
This computer has no local network address, so there is nothing for a phone to scan.
On the other devices, pick Be a sink; if one does not connect by itself, scan this code.
A phone that scans it will connect to %1$s
%1$s %2$d is taken. Is the command-line host, or another SoundMesh, still open?
The computer\'s speakers will not open: %1$s
Cannot announce this host on the local network, so phones will not find it: %1$s
Getting ready to look for the host…
Found a host, but the versions do not match. Both sides need the same version.
There are two hosts in the room. Close one first.
Looking for the host; none has answered yet. Make sure there is a host on the local network. If it cannot connect, type the address directly.
Connecting to the host (trying every 3 s)…
Last time the host did not answer the clock, so this device did not connect.
Last time this device did not connect: %1$s
Syncing the clock with the host…
The host has gone quiet and may have dropped. This device plays by itself when the host plays again.
The host is measuring, and this computer is taking part…
Measuring: leave the devices alone and keep it quiet.
Delivered. %1$d in the room, %2$d pairs measured for this computer.

Delivered. %1$d in the room, %2$d pairs measured for this computer. This computer has never been properly synced with the host, so the %3$.3f ms this round worked out has been kept to be going on with. It is an estimate, out by 1–2 ms. When there is time, pick this computer on the host\'s list and sync the pair; a real measurement will replace it.
This network is too slow to align on: a round trip to the host takes %1$.0f ms, and past %2$.0f nothing lines up.
This computer has no microphone, so it cannot measure. The host will say \"no microphone\".
Windows is keeping the microphone from this app: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, and turn on \"Let desktop apps access your microphone\".
The microphone runs at %1$s and measuring needs 48 kHz: set it to 48000 Hz in Sound settings.
Measure the distances between the devices
Put the phones where you want to hear them
This computer has no microphone, so it cannot measure.
Measuring; playing waits until it is done.
The computer\'s 0.5 m to you is assumed, not measured.
